questions.question: State Newton's law of gravitation. What is the gravitational constant G?
questions.solution:

questions.knowledgeNote: G is one of the least precisely known constants. Gravitational force is always attractive and acts along the line joining the particles.
questions.answer: **Newton's law of gravitation:** every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force **directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres**, acting along the line joining them: **F = Gm₁m₂/r²**. **Gravitational constant G:** the universal constant of proportionality in the law — the gravitational force between two unit masses separated by unit distance. Its value is **G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²** (measured by Cavendish). It is universal: the same for any pair of masses anywhere. **Deep point:** G is not g — G is the universal coupling constant of gravity, while g is the local field strength; they meet in g = GM/R².
